result.target_topic: Limitations of Remaining Performance Obligations as Forward-Looking Indicator
result.target_summary: Because the majority of Avago's revenue comes from contracts with a duration of one year or less, the disclosed remaining performance obligations are not indicative of revenue for future periods.

target_year_over_year_context.explanation: Both disclosures address Remaining Performance Obligations under Note 3. The 2023 disclosure (D066) states obligations are not indicative of future revenue because customers generally do not exercise termination rights and most contracts are one year or less. The 2024 disclosure (D068) provides a similar caveat that obligations are not indicative of future revenue because the majority of revenue is from contracts with a duration of one year or less. They share the specific subject of the reliability of RPO disclosure based on contract duration/termination behavior.

materiality_analysis.reason: The 2024 disclosure reduces the explanatory caveat for RPOs. The 2023 version cited both lack of termination rights and short contract durations. The 2024 version cites only short contract durations. However, the core message—that RPOs are not indicative of future revenue due to the nature of the contracts (short duration)—remains unchanged. The removal of the specific reference to termination rights appears to be a refinement or simplification rather than a material change in risk or operational reality, as the primary driver (short duration) remains constant.

materiality_analysis.reason: The disclosure introduces a significant change in financial position and operational scale, with Remaining Performance Obligations increasing by approximately 63% from $20.5 billion to $33.3 billion. While the percentage recognized within 12 months decreased slightly (43% to 35%), the absolute magnitude of the backlog represents a meaningful expansion in committed future revenue. Additionally, the text was restructured to explicitly state that customers do not have termination rights for the contracts included in the $33.3B figure, clarifying the quality of the backlog compared to the previous year's disclosure which noted customers generally did not exercise such rights.

comparisons.peer_topic: Remaining Performance Obligations Balance and Recognition
comparisons.peer_summary: As of December 28, 2024, the aggregate transaction price allocated to remaining performance obligations under contracts with an original expected duration of more than one year was $85 million, of which $67 million is expected to be recognized in the next 12 months.
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and AMD disclose remaining performance obligations for contracts with durations exceeding one year and explicitly note that their revenue patterns or obligations are predominantly short-term, limiting the forward-looking utility of these balances. AVGO states that because the majority of its revenue is from contracts of one year or less, remaining obligations are not indicative of future revenue. AMD reports a specific balance ($85 million) for obligations over one year and similarly discloses that amounts with original expected durations of one year or less are excluded from this figure.

sentences.text: In addition, the majority of our revenue is from contracts with a duration of one year or less.
Accordingly, our remaining performance obligations disclosed above are not indicative of revenue for future periods.

As of December 28, 2024, the aggregate transaction price allocated to remaining performance obligations under contracts with an original expected duration of more than one year was $85 million, of which $67 million is expected to be recognized in the next 12 months.
The revenue allocated to remaining performance obligations does not include amounts which have an original expected duration of one year or less.

comparisons.peer_topic: Revenue Recognition Policy and Contract Terms
comparisons.peer_summary: Revenue is recognized at a point in time when control transfers, primarily for short-term contracts at fixed prices, though some contracts have performance obligations extending beyond one year.
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and MU highlight that the majority of their contractual revenue relationships are short-term, which impacts the significance of long-term performance obligations. AVGO discloses that the majority of its revenue comes from contracts with a duration of one year or less. Similarly, MU states that substantially all contracts are short-term in duration at fixed prices, although it acknowledges that some performance obligations may extend beyond one year.
